evidence: Constructor injects StartSubscription, ChangeSeats and CancelSubscription from src/application/use-cases. These are application-layer types that infrastructure may depend on, so this is wiring.
create(body: StartBody) only returns this.start.execute(body.customerId, body.plan, body.seats), with no validation or calculation.
resize(id, body: SeatsBody) only returns this.changeSeats.execute(id, body.seats), with no seat-limit logic.
cancel(id, body: CancelBody) only passes body.reason to this.cancelSubscription.execute and returns the result.
Candidate flag cohesion/low-cohesion (LCOM4 3): each method uses a separate injected use case, which is normal for a controller. It is not a misplaced responsibility under this rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/http/SubscriptionController.ts is a thin infrastructure (delivery) adapter, and it holds no business rules. It declares request body shapes (StartBody, SeatsBody, CancelBody). Its constructor receives application use cases, which counts as dependency wiring because infrastructure may depend on the application layer. Each method only maps body fields onto a use-case execute() call and returns what that call returns, with no checks, calculations or decisions of its own. Seat-count validation, plan logic and cancellation rules all stay inside the application use cases. The cohesion flag (LCOM4 = 3) does not hold up as a finding: each controller method calling a different injected use case is normal for a controller, and it has nothing to do with this layer-role rule.
